items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

ctx.x: No. I played piano at Peabody. And I was six years old, and I studied there, this was in 1946. My mother used to send me downtown on the bus by myself. It was perfectly safe. There was a statue in downtown Baltimore of a guy riding a horse, an English guy riding a horse with his arm out like this. My mother said, “When you see the horse and the guy pointing, Peabody’s right — he’s pointing right at Peabody. Get off the next block.” I did. It was fine. The only trouble was is I, for whatever reason, didn’t like to…
Kind of like Marty Grosz. That style of — © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-

Exactly. Exactly. And then the bass came along, and Ray Brown entered my life with Oscar Peterson at the Stratford Shakespearean Festival, the record I think they recorded in ‘52, and that became the Holy Grail. That became the reason for living was that music for me. I mean it’s amazing how powerful that music was to me. I never heard anything swing that like, I never heard arrangements like that, freedom, joy, everything expressed. Everything that I wanted out of this life was in that record, so I quickly…
